channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [6] Non-local synchronization of continuous time crystals in a semiconductor
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Markus Betz, Manfred Bayer

Authors: Alex Greilich, Nataliia E. Kopteva, Vladimir L. Korenev, et al.

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Experimental study of collective spin behavior and time crystals in a real semiconductor system.

Tags: #semiconductor #spin-dynamics #quantum-matter

Abstract: Synchronization of weakly coupled oscillators is a widespread phenomenon underlying collective behavior in physical and biological systems. Here, the authors demonstrate mutual synchronization of auto oscillating electron–nuclear spin ensembles in a semiconductor, showing frequency locking over tens of micrometers mediated by electron spin diffusion.
